sentences.text: The genus is based on a partial juvenile skeleton that was previously classified as Thecodontosaurus.
Pantydraco had a long tail that tapered at the end but was broad at the hip joint.
Its forelimbs were adapted for grasping, while its hindlimbs supported its body weight.
The hands possessed three movable digits with a fourth digit embedded within them.
Juvenile fossils of Pantydraco are estimated to have been between 0.7 and 1 meter tall.
Adult Pantydraco are believed to have reached a length of about 3 meters.
The estimated weight for an average adult Pantydraco is about 50 kilograms.
The fossil material used to describe Pantydraco had been known in scientific literature since 1983.
The fossils were originally discovered in 1952 by Kermack and Robinson.
Adam Yates named the species Thecodontosaurus caducus in 2003 based on fossil material NHMUK PV RUP 24.
The genus Pantydraco was established by Galton, Yates, and Kermack in 2007.
Researchers consider Pantydraco to have been probably omnivorous, representing a transition from carnivory to herbivory.
It is probable that Pantydraco walked bipedally.
Pantydraco is classified within the superorder Dinosauria, order Saurischia, and suborder Sauropodomorpha.
Pantydraco is generally considered basal within Sauropodomorpha, closely related to Thecodontosaurus.
Pantydraco lived during the Late Triassic, approximately 204 million years ago in the Rhaetian stage, in what is now Europe.
The time range for Pantydraco is estimated from 237 to 227.3 million years ago during the Carnian stage.
The region where Pantydraco lived was a characteristic wetland during the Triassic period.
